metadata.title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption without Bootstrapping
metadata.authors: Zvika Brakerski, Craig Gentry, Vinod Vaikuntanathan
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Leveled Fully Homomorphic Encryption
nodes.statement: A family $\{E^{(L)} : L \in \mathbb{Z}^+\}$ is leveled fully homomorphic if all $E^{(L)}$ share the same decryption circuit, $E^{(L)}$ compactly evaluates all circuits of depth $\le L$, and complexity is polynomial in $\lambda$, $L$, and circuit size.
nodes.statement_clean: A family of FHE schemes parameterized by depth L sharing one decryption circuit and able to evaluate any depth-L circuit compactly.

nodes.name: Learning with Errors (LWE)
nodes.statement: For parameters $n, q, \chi$, distinguish $(a_i, b_i)$ uniform in $\mathbb{Z}_q^{n+1}$ from $(a_i, \langle a_i, s\rangle + e_i)$ for $s \in \mathbb{Z}_q^n$ uniform and $e_i \leftarrow \chi$.
nodes.statement_clean: Decision problem of distinguishing noisy linear samples from uniform samples over $\mathbb{Z}_q$.

nodes.name: B-bounded distribution
nodes.statement: A distribution ensemble $\{\chi_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ is $B$-bounded if $\Pr_{e \leftarrow \chi_n}[|e| > B] = \mathrm{negl}(n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: A distribution where samples exceed $B$ with negligible probability.

nodes.name: Ring Learning with Errors (RLWE)
nodes.statement: Let $f(x) = x^d + 1$ with $d$ a power of 2, $R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(f(x))$, $R_q = R/qR$. Distinguish $(a_i, b_i)$ uniform in $R_q^2$ from $(a_i, a_i \cdot s + e_i)$ for $s \leftarrow R_q$ and $e_i \leftarrow \chi$.
nodes.statement_clean: The ring analogue of LWE, with samples in $R_q$ for the cyclotomic ring $R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(x^d+1)$.

nodes.name: General Learning with Errors (GLWE)
nodes.statement: For $n, f, q, \chi$ with $R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(f(x))$, distinguish uniform $(a_i, b_i) \in R_q^{n+1}$ from $(a_i, \langle a_i, s\rangle + e_i)$ with $s \leftarrow R_q^n$, $a_i \leftarrow R_q^n$, $e_i \leftarrow \chi$. LWE is GLWE with $d=1$; RLWE is GLWE with $n=1$.
nodes.statement_clean: A unified problem that interpolates between LWE ($d=1$) and RLWE ($n=1$).

nodes.name: Scale (modulus-switching primitive)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Scale}(x, q, p, r)$ returns the $R$-vector $x'$ closest to $(p/q) \cdot x$ such that $x' \equiv x \pmod{r}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Rounded scaling that approximately multiplies a vector by $p/q$ while preserving residue mod $r$.

nodes.name: Ring $\ell_1$-norm
nodes.statement: For $s \in R^n$ with $R$ a ring, $\ell_1^{(R)}(s) = \sum_i \|s[i]\|$, the sum of coefficient norms.
nodes.statement_clean: Sum of (Euclidean) norms of the entries of a vector over the ring $R$.

nodes.name: BitDecomp
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{BitDecomp}(x, q)$ writes $x = \sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor\log q\rfloor} 2^j u_j$ with $u_j \in R_2^n$ and returns $(u_0, u_1, \ldots, u_{\lfloor\log q\rfloor}) \in R_2^{n \cdot \lceil\log q\rceil}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Decomposes a vector mod $q$ into its base-2 bit-vector representation.

nodes.name: Powersof2
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Powersof2}(x, q) = (x, 2x, 4x, \ldots, 2^{\lfloor\log q\rfloor} x) \in R_q^{n \cdot \lceil\log q\rceil}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Stacks scaled copies of $x$ by successive powers of 2 up to $q$.

nodes.name: Expansion factor of a ring
nodes.statement: $\gamma_R = \max\{\|a \cdot b\| / (\|a\|\|b\|) : a, b \in R\}$. For $R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(x^d+1)$, $\gamma_R \le \sqrt{d}$ by Cauchy-Schwarz.
nodes.statement_clean: Worst-case multiplicative blow-up of norm under ring multiplication.

nodes.name: Noise of a ciphertext
nodes.statement: For ciphertext $c$ and key $s$, the noise is $[\langle c, s\rangle]_q$. Decryption succeeds while $|[\langle c, s\rangle]_q| < q/2$; the message is $m = [[\langle c, s\rangle]_q]_2$.
nodes.statement_clean: The reduced inner product $[\langle c, s\rangle]_q$, whose magnitude must stay below $q/2$ for correct decryption.

nodes.name: Regev worst-case to average-case reduction for LWE
nodes.statement: For any $n$, prime $q = q(n)$, $B \ge 2\sqrt{n}$, there is an efficiently samplable $B$-bounded $\chi$ such that solving $\mathrm{LWE}_{n,q,\chi}$ implies an efficient quantum algorithm for $\tilde{O}(qn^{1.5}/B)$-approximate worst-case SIVP and gapSVP.
nodes.statement_clean: Hardness of LWE follows (quantumly) from worst-case hardness of approximate lattice problems.
conclusions: Efficient $\mathrm{LWE}_{n,q,\chi}$ solver implies efficient quantum solver for $\tilde{O}(qn^{1.5}/B)$-approximate SIVP and gapSVP

nodes.name: Lyubashevsky-Peikert-Regev RLWE-to-ideal-SVP reduction
nodes.statement: For $d$ a power of 2, $R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(x^d+1)$, prime $q \equiv 1 \pmod d$, $B = \omega(\sqrt{d \log d})$, there is a samplable $\chi$ such that solving $\mathrm{RLWE}_{d,q,\chi}$ yields a quantum algorithm for $d^{\omega(1)} \cdot (q/B)$-approximate worst-case ideal-SVP over $R$.
nodes.statement_clean: RLWE is at least as hard as approximating short vectors in ideal lattices.

nodes.name: Modulus switching (informal, integer case)
nodes.statement: Let $p, q$ be odd moduli and $c$ an integer vector. Define $c'$ as the integer vector closest to $(p/q) c$ with $c' \equiv c \pmod 2$. For any $s$ with $|[\langle c, s\rangle]_q| < q/2 - (q/p) \cdot \ell_1(s)$, $[\langle c', s\rangle]_p \equiv [\langle c, s\rangle]_q \pmod 2$ and $|[\langle c', s\rangle]_p| < (p/q) \cdot |[\langle c, s\rangle]_q| + \ell_1(s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Switching from modulus $q$ to $p$ via rounded scaling preserves the message bit and shrinks noise by roughly a factor $p/q$.

nodes.name: BitDecomp/Powersof2 inner product identity
nodes.statement: For vectors $c, s$ of equal length, $\langle \mathrm{BitDecomp}(c, q), \mathrm{Powersof2}(s, q)\rangle = \langle c, s\rangle \pmod q$.
nodes.statement_clean: The bit-decomposition of $c$ paired with the powers-of-2 lift of $s$ recovers $\langle c, s\rangle$ mod $q$.

nodes.name: Correctness of key switching
nodes.statement: Let $A \cdot s_2 = 2 e_2 \in R_q^N$, $c_1 \in R_q^{n_1}$, and $c_2 \leftarrow \mathrm{SwitchKey}(\tau_{s_1 \to s_2}, c_1)$. Then $\langle c_2, s_2\rangle = 2 \langle \mathrm{BitDecomp}(c_1), e_2\rangle + \langle c_1, s_1\rangle \pmod q$.
nodes.statement_clean: Key switching produces a ciphertext under $s_2$ whose noise grows only by a small additive term.
conclusions: $\langle c_2, s_2\rangle = 2\langle \mathrm{BitDecomp}(c_1), e_2\rangle + \langle c_1, s_1\rangle \pmod q$

nodes.name: Modulus switching (general ring version)
nodes.statement: Let $q > p > r$ with $q \equiv p \equiv 1 \pmod r$, $c \in R^n$, $c' \leftarrow \mathrm{Scale}(c, q, p, r)$. If $\|[\langle c, s\rangle]_q\| < q/2 - (q/p)(r/2)\sqrt{d}\,\gamma_R\,\ell_1^{(R)}(s)$, then $[\langle c', s\rangle]_p \equiv [\langle c, s\rangle]_q \pmod r$ and $\|[\langle c', s\rangle]_p\| < (p/q)\|[\langle c, s\rangle]_q\| + (r/2)\sqrt{d}\,\gamma_R\,\ell_1^{(R)}(s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: General-ring version of Lemma 1: rounded modulus switching preserves the residue mod $r$ and contracts noise by $p/q$.

nodes.name: Noise reduction by modulus switching without bootstrapping
nodes.statement: If $c$ encrypts $m$ under $s$ for modulus $q$ and $\|e_q\| = \|[\langle c, s\rangle]_q\| < q/2 - (q/p)(r/2)\sqrt d \gamma_R \ell_1^{(R)}(s)$, then $c' \leftarrow \mathrm{Scale}(c, q, p, r)$ encrypts $m$ under $s$ for modulus $p$ with $\|e_p\| \le (p/q)\|e_q\| + \gamma_R(r/2)\sqrt d \,\ell_1^{(R)}(s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: An evaluator can shrink ciphertext noise by switching to a smaller modulus, without ever knowing $s$.

nodes.name: Initial noise of FHE.Enc
nodes.statement: With $n_L, q_L$ the FHE.Enc parameters and $B_\chi$ a high-probability bound on $\chi$-samples, the noise of fresh ciphertexts has length at most $1 + 2 \gamma_R \sqrt d ((2 n_L + 1) \log q_L) B_\chi$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bounds the magnitude of the noise produced by the encryption algorithm in terms of $\gamma_R, d, n_L, q_L, B_\chi$.

nodes.name: Correctness of FHE.Add (pre-Refresh)
nodes.statement: If $c_1, c_2$ encrypt $m_1, m_2$ under $s_j$ with noise $\le B$, and $c_3$ is the zero-padded sum interpreted under $s_j' = s_j \otimes s_j$, then $\|[\langle c_3, s_j'\rangle]_{q_j}\| \le 2B$, and if $2B < q_j/2$ then $c_3$ encrypts $m_1 + m_2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Homomorphic addition at most doubles the noise.
assumptions: $c_3 = c_1 + c_2$ padded and reinterpreted under $s_j'$

nodes.name: Correctness of FHE.Mult (pre-Refresh)
nodes.statement: If $c_1, c_2$ encrypt $m_1, m_2$ under $s_j$ with noise $\le B$, and $c_3$ is the coefficient vector of $L^{\mathrm{long}}_{c_1, c_2}(x \otimes x)$, then $\|[\langle c_3, s_j'\rangle]_{q_j}\| \le \gamma_R B^2$, and if $\gamma_R B^2 < q_j/2$ then $c_3$ encrypts $m_1 \cdot m_2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Homomorphic multiplication produces a long ciphertext under $s_j \otimes s_j$ whose noise is at most $\gamma_R B^2$.
conclusions: $\gamma_R B^2 < q_j/2 \Rightarrow [[\langle c_3, s_j'\rangle]_{q_j}]_2 = m_1 \cdot m_2$

nodes.name: Correctness of Switch-Moduli step
nodes.statement: Let $c_1$ be under $s_j'' = \mathrm{BitDecomp}(s_j \otimes s_j, q_j)$ with $\|e_j\| \le B$ and $c_2 \leftarrow \mathrm{Scale}(c_1, q_j, q_{j-1}, 2)$. Then $\|e_{j-1}\| \le (q_{j-1}/q_j) B + d \gamma_R \binom{n_j+1}{2} \lceil \log q_j\rceil$, and decryption is preserved if this is $< q_{j-1}/2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bounds the noise of a ciphertext after switching from modulus $q_j$ down to $q_{j-1}$.

nodes.name: Correctness of Switch-Key step
nodes.statement: Let $c_2$ be under $s_j''$ for modulus $q_{j-1}$ with $\|e_1\| \le B$ and $c_3 \leftarrow \mathrm{SwitchKey}(\tau_{s_j'' \to s_{j-1}}, c_2, q_{j-1})$. Then $\|e_2\| \le B + 2 \gamma_R \binom{n_j+1}{2}\lceil \log q_j\rceil^2 \sqrt d \, B_\chi$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bounds the additional noise introduced by the SwitchKey procedure.

nodes.name: Leveled FHE without Bootstrapping (main theorem)
nodes.statement: For some $\mu = \theta(\log\lambda + \log L)$, FHE is a correct $L$-leveled FHE scheme over $R_2$ with per-gate computation $\tilde{O}(d \cdot n_L^3 \cdot L^2)$. For LWE ($d=1$): $\tilde{O}(\lambda^3 L^5)$. For RLWE ($n=1$): $\tilde{O}(\lambda \cdot L^3)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Main result: there is a leveled FHE scheme without bootstrapping; under RLWE its per-gate cost is $\tilde{O}(\lambda L^3)$.
assumptions: GLWE is hard with the chosen parameters
Properties 1 and 2 of Section 4.4 hold for the modulus ladder
conclusions: FHE is correct for depth-$L$ arithmetic circuits over $R_2$

nodes.name: Batched FHE on plaintext slots
nodes.statement: Let $p \equiv 1 \pmod{2d}$ be a polynomial-size prime. The RLWE-based FHE on $R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(x^d+1)$ adapts to plaintext space $R_p \cong \bigotimes_{i=1}^d R_{\mathfrak p_i}$ with same asymptotic performance, and homomorphically evaluates a depth-$L$ boolean circuit $f$ on $\ell$ inputs with per-gate cost $\tilde{O}(\lambda L^3 / \min\{d, \ell\})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Batching via Chinese Remaindering across the $d$ prime ideals gives polylogarithmic per-gate cost when $\ell \ge \lambda$.

nodes.name: Optimal lazy-bootstrapping interval
nodes.statement: Let $f(\lambda, L) = \lambda^{a_1} L^{a_2}$ and $g(\lambda, L) = \lambda^{b_1} L^{b_2}$ with $b_1 > a_1$, $b_2 > a_2 \ge 1$. For $h(\lambda, L) = f(\lambda, L) + g(\lambda, c+L)/L$ with $c = \theta(\log\lambda)$, $h$ is minimized at some $L \in [(c-1)/(b_2-1), c/(b_2-1)]$, i.e. $L = \theta(\log\lambda)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bootstrapping every $\theta(\log\lambda)$ levels minimizes per-gate cost for the assumed cost models.

nodes.name: Modulus switching with ideal moduli
nodes.statement: Let $q_1, q_2$ be $\alpha$-good with $\|q_1\| < \|q_2\|$, $B_I$ a short basis of an ideal $I$ with $q_1 - q_2 \in I$, $c'\leftarrow \mathrm{Scale}(c, q_2, q_1, I)$. If $\|[\langle c, s\rangle]_{q_2}\|$ is below an explicit threshold, then $[\langle c', s\rangle]_{q_1} \equiv [\langle c, s\rangle]_{q_2} \pmod I$ with bounded noise growth controlled by $\alpha(d), \gamma_R, r_{B_I, \mathrm{out}}, \ell_1^{(R)}(s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalizes Lemma 4 from integer to ideal moduli, enabling exponentially large prime plaintext spaces.
nodes.notes: Statement abbreviated; PDF garbling on the inequality bounds. See paper Lemma 11 for the exact thresholds.

nodes.name: Basic GLWE-Based Encryption Scheme (E)
nodes.statement: GLWE-based public-key encryption with no homomorphic operations: setup, key generation, encryption (as $c = m + A^T r$), and decryption (as $m = [[\langle c, s\rangle]_q]_2$).

nodes.name: Key Switching (SwitchKeyGen / SwitchKey)
nodes.statement: Translates a ciphertext under $s_1$ to one under $s_2$ encrypting the same message, using $\tau_{s_1 \to s_2} = A + \mathrm{Powersof2}(s_1)$ where $A \cdot s_2 = 2 e_2$.

nodes.name: FHE Scheme without Bootstrapping
nodes.statement: Leveled FHE built from a ladder of moduli $q_L > q_{L-1} > \cdots > q_0$ and per-level keys $\{s_j\}$. Add and Mult operate at level $j$, then $\mathrm{FHE.Refresh}$ moves the result down to level $j-1$.
output: Algorithms FHE.Enc, FHE.Dec, FHE.Add, FHE.Mult, FHE.Refresh

nodes.name: FHE.Refresh
nodes.statement: Three-step noise-management procedure that turns a ciphertext under $s_j' = s_j \otimes s_j$ at modulus $q_j$ into a ciphertext under $s_{j-1}$ at modulus $q_{j-1}$ via Powersof2 expansion, modulus rescaling, and key switching.

nodes.name: Pack / Unpack (for batched bootstrapping)
nodes.statement: Pack aggregates $d$ ciphertexts $c_i$ each in plaintext slot $\mathfrak p_1$ into one ciphertext spread over slots $\mathfrak p_1, \ldots, \mathfrak p_d$ via the automorphisms $\sigma_{1 \to i}$ and SwitchKey. Unpack reverses this using $\sigma_{i \to 1}$ and a short element $u \in 1 + \mathfrak p_1$ with $u \in \mathfrak p_j$ for $j \ne 1$.
input: Ciphertexts $c_1, \ldots, c_d$ (Pack) or single batched ciphertext $c$ (Unpack)
output: Or unpacked ciphertexts $c_1^*, \ldots, c_d^*$ all in slot $\mathfrak p_1$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 (informal modulus switching)
nodes.statement: Let $[\langle c, s\rangle]_q = \langle c, s\rangle - kq$ for some integer $k$, set $e_p = \langle c', s\rangle - kp$. Show $e_p$ has small enough norm to equal $[\langle c', s\rangle]_p$, and that $e_p \equiv [\langle c, s\rangle]_q \pmod 2$ since $c' \equiv c$ and $p \equiv q \pmod 2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2 (BitDecomp/Powersof2 identity)
nodes.statement: Expand $\mathrm{BitDecomp}(c, q) = (u_0, \ldots, u_{\lfloor\log q\rfloor})$ and use bilinearity: $\sum_j \langle u_j, 2^j s\rangle = \langle \sum_j 2^j u_j, s\rangle = \langle c, s\rangle$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3 (key switching correctness)
nodes.statement: $\langle c_2, s_2\rangle = \mathrm{BitDecomp}(c_1)^T B s_2 = \mathrm{BitDecomp}(c_1)^T (2 e_2 + \mathrm{Powersof2}(s_1)) = 2\langle \mathrm{BitDecomp}(c_1), e_2\rangle + \langle c_1, s_1\rangle$ by Lemma 2.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4 (modulus switching, ring version)
nodes.statement: Write $[\langle c, s\rangle]_q = \langle c, s\rangle - kq$, define $e_p = \langle c', s\rangle - kp$. Show $\|e_p\| \le (p/q)\|[\langle c, s\rangle]_q\| + \gamma_R(r/2)\sqrt d \,\ell_1^{(R)}(s) < p/2$, hence $e_p = [\langle c', s\rangle]_p$, and the residue mod $r$ matches $[\langle c, s\rangle]_q$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 (parameter setting)
nodes.statement: Choose a universal noise bound $B = \lambda^a L^b$ and moduli $q_j \approx 2^{(j+1)\omega(\log\lambda + \log L)}$ so Properties 1 and 2 (noise dominates additive errors; ratio $q_j/q_{j-1} \ge 2 B \gamma_R$) hold; induct on circuit level to keep noise bounded.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 10 (lazy bootstrapping interval)
nodes.statement: $h(\lambda, L) \to \infty$ as $L \to 0$ and as $L \to \infty$, so it has a positive minimum. The derivative analysis shows the negative-derivative region of $g(\lambda, c+L)/L$ ends at $L = c/(b_2 - 1)$ and dominates $f$'s positive derivative for $L < (c-1)/(b_2 - 1)$, pinning the optimum to $L = \theta(\log\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Choose universal noise bound and modulus ladder
nodes.statement: Pick $B = \lambda^a L^b$ for large constants $a, b$, and $q_j \approx 2^{(j+1) \cdot \omega(\log\lambda + \log L)}$; equivalently $q_j$ has $(j+1)\mu$ bits with $\mu = \theta(\log\lambda + \log L)$.

nodes.name: Verify Property 1 (noise dominates additive errors)
nodes.statement: Show $B \ge 2(\eta_{\mathrm{Scale}, j} + \eta_{\mathrm{SwitchKey}, j})$, using that both additive terms are polynomial in $\lambda$ and $\log q_L$, hence in $\lambda$ and $L$.

nodes.name: Verify Property 2 (modulus ratio dominates noise blow-up)
nodes.statement: Show $q_j / q_{j-1} \ge 2 B \gamma_R$, using that the ratio is super-polynomial in $\lambda$ and $L$.

nodes.name: Inductive step: noise after FHE.Mult stays $\le B$
nodes.statement: Assuming the noise of $c_1, c_2$ at level $j$ is $\le B$, after multiplication and Refresh the noise is $\le (q_{j-1}/q_j) \gamma_R B^2 + \eta_{\mathrm{Scale}, j} + \eta_{\mathrm{SwitchKey}, j} \le \frac{1}{2 B \gamma_R}\gamma_R B^2 + \frac{1}{2} B = B$.

nodes.name: Expand
nodes.statement: Set $c_1 \leftarrow \mathrm{Powersof2}(c, q_j)$. Then $\langle c_1, s_j''\rangle \equiv \langle c, s_j'\rangle \pmod{q_j}$ by Lemma 2; noise unchanged.

nodes.name: Switch Moduli
nodes.statement: Set $c_2 \leftarrow \mathrm{Scale}(c_1, q_j, q_{j-1}, 2)$, a ciphertext under $s_j''$ at modulus $q_{j-1}$ with noise contracted by $\approx q_{j-1}/q_j$.

nodes.name: Switch Keys
nodes.statement: Output $c_3 \leftarrow \mathrm{SwitchKey}(\tau_{s_j'' \to s_{j-1}}, c_2, q_{j-1})$, a ciphertext under $s_{j-1}$ at modulus $q_{j-1}$.

nodes.name: FHE.Setup ladder of moduli
nodes.statement: Run $\mathrm{params}_j \leftarrow E.\mathrm{Setup}(1^\lambda, 1^{(j+1)\mu}, b)$ for $j = L, \ldots, 0$, then unify ring dimension and noise distribution to $d_L, \chi_L$.

nodes.name: FHE.KeyGen with key-switching hints
nodes.statement: For $j = L, \ldots, 0$: generate $s_j, A_j$, form $s_j' = s_j \otimes s_j$, $s_j'' = \mathrm{BitDecomp}(s_j', q_j)$, then $\tau_{s_j'' \to s_{j-1}} \leftarrow \mathrm{SwitchKeyGen}(s_j'', s_{j-1})$ (skip at $j=L$).

nodes.name: FHE.Add
nodes.statement: $c_3 \leftarrow c_1 + c_2 \pmod{q_j}$ (interpreted under $s_j'$), then $c_4 \leftarrow \mathrm{FHE.Refresh}(c_3, \tau_{s_j'' \to s_{j-1}}, q_j, q_{j-1})$.

nodes.name: FHE.Mult
nodes.statement: Compute $c_3$ as the coefficient vector of $L^{\mathrm{long}}_{c_1, c_2}(x \otimes x)$, then $c_4 \leftarrow \mathrm{FHE.Refresh}(c_3, \tau_{s_j'' \to s_{j-1}}, q_j, q_{j-1})$.

nodes.name: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE)
nodes.statement: Construct an encryption scheme that allows arbitrarily many homomorphic Add and Mult evaluations on encrypted data without access to the secret key, with provable security and bounded per-gate computation overhead.
nodes.statement_clean: The central problem of evaluating arbitrary circuits on ciphertexts.

nodes.name: Refresh need not follow each addition
nodes.statement: Since addition increases noise much more slowly than multiplication, one need not refresh after additions, even high fan-in ones.

nodes.name: Why the scheme is genuinely 'without bootstrapping'
nodes.statement: Although $\tau_{s_j'' \to s_{j-1}}$ resembles an encrypted secret key and SwitchKey resembles homomorphic decryption, SwitchKey runs in quasi-linear time (below the quadratic lower bound for bootstrapping), is not based on a boolean decryption circuit, and the actual noise reduction comes from the Scale step, not from SwitchKey.

nodes.name: Decryption equation
nodes.statement: $m = [[\langle c, s\rangle]_q]_2$

nodes.name: Public-key relation $A s = 2 e$
nodes.statement: $A \cdot s = 2 e$, where $A$ is the $(N \times (n+1))$ public-key matrix and $s = (1, s')$.

nodes.name: Encryption equation
nodes.statement: $c \leftarrow m + A^T r \in R_q^{n+1}$ for $r \in R_2^N$ and message $m = (m, 0, \ldots, 0)$.

nodes.name: GLWE hardness assumption
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{GLWE}_{n, f, q, \chi}$ is infeasible: the noisy distribution and the uniform distribution are computationally indistinguishable. Believed hard whenever $n \cdot d = \Omega(\lambda \log(q/B))$.

nodes.name: Circular security (for unbounded FHE / single key)
nodes.statement: It is safe to encrypt the leveled FHE secret key under its own public key. Used to obtain pure FHE from leveled FHE and to allow a single key $\{s_j\} = s$ across levels.
